title: The unique common-stage internal Hom arrow and its representative calculus
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $W$. Use the permitted pairs, literal output objects and normalized comparisons of [def-weil-common-stage-internal-hom-data]. For every arrow between two permitted pairs, all its common finite-stage representatives give exactly one output arrow. The output of an identity representative is the identity, and the output of the composite of two representatives is the composite of their outputs, with the first input coordinate composed in reversed order. These assertions use the single-extension equation of [lem-weil-common-stage-internal-hom-representative] only to establish representative independence; they do not assert the existence or uniqueness of a descended functor.

source.place: The commonStageDerivedInternalHom_existsUnique proof plan: common representatives, unique output arrows, rational Hom identity/composition, and cancellation of the middle comparison.

proof.text: Apply the existing StageSystem common-stage representative lemma to the reversed first coordinate and the forward second coordinate. Enlarge above both literal output composita and the requested lower bound. Full-subcategory morphism extensionality combines the two representatives.

Use representative independence to show that the displayed conjugated output from any one representative is characterized by its value on every representative. Any two arrows with that characterization agree by evaluation on one representative. Choose this uniquely determined arrow, and derive its representative formula.

The identity representative maps to the identity by rational Hom functoriality and the endpoint inverse law. At one common stage, the first input composes in reverse order and the second in forward order. Rational Hom preserves this product composite, and the middle scalar comparison cancels with its inverse. The StageSystem identity, composition and further-transport representative equations give precisely the stated quotient-arrow formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem homArrow_existsUnique (W : Scheme.{u})
    (P Q : (commonStageHomPairs.{u, v} l Ω W).FullSubcategory) (f : P ⟶ Q) :
    ∃! g : commonStageHomObject l Ω W P ⟶ commonStageHomObject l Ω W Q,
      ∀ (L : Index l Ω)
        (h : (commonStageHomObject l Ω W P).stage ≤ L)
        (h' : (commonStageHomObject l Ω W Q).stage ≤ L)
        (a : (commonStageHomPairAtStage l Ω W Q L h').obj.1.unop ⟶
          (commonStageHomPairAtStage l Ω W P L h).obj.1.unop)
        (b : (commonStageHomPairAtStage l Ω W P L h).obj.2 ⟶
          (commonStageHomPairAtStage l Ω W Q L h').obj.2),
        f = input l Ω W P Q L h h' a b → g = output l Ω W P Q L h h' a b
